review.source: Actual written N1904 and original Berean publisher rows, reviewed against displayed BSB; distinct peer pending.

4:1.sourceText: Τότε ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἀνήχθη εἰς τὴν ἔρημον ὑπὸ τοῦ Πνεύματος, πειρασθῆναι ὑπὸ τοῦ διαβόλου.
4:1.targetText: Then Jesus was led by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

4:2.sourceText: καὶ νηστεύσας ἡμέρας τεσσεράκοντα καὶ τεσσεράκοντα νύκτας ὕστερον ἐπείνασεν.
4:2.targetText: After fasting forty days and forty nights, He was hungry.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening connective is omitted. The actual afterward adverb is implicit because English frames fasting as the preceding event.

4:3.sourceText: καὶ προσελθὼν ὁ πειράζων εἶπεν αὐτῷ Εἰ Υἱὸς εἶ τοῦ Θεοῦ, εἰπὲ ἵνα οἱ λίθοι οὗτοι ἄρτοι γένωνται.
4:3.targetText: The tempter came to Him and said, “If You are the Son of God, tell these stones to become bread.”

groups.note: The actual purpose/content conjunction with becoming subjunctive is expressed by an English infinitive.

studyHeads.note: Infinitival link expresses the actual content conjunction in this recast.
Actual becoming verb is the lexical head.

unmappedSource.reason: The initial narrative coordinator is absent. English introduces its own coordination between approaching and saying.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English coordinates the two written events where actual approaching is a participle.
English supplies the article in Son of God. The written genitive article attaches to God.

4:4.sourceText: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν Γέγραπται Οὐκ ἐπ’ ἄρτῳ μόνῳ ζήσεται ὁ ἄνθρωπος, ἀλλ’ ἐπὶ παντὶ ῥήματι ἐκπορευομένῳ διὰ στόματος Θεοῦ.
4:4.targetText: But Jesus answered, “It is written:  ‘Man shall not live on bread alone, but on every word that comes from the mouth of God.’”

groups.note: The actual answering participle and said finite are expressed by the single English answering predicate.

studyHeads.note: The actual answering participle carries the lexical content.

groups.note: Actual future living supplies the English auxiliary and lexical verb. The written negator is separately linked.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the contextually identified speaker. The actual subject is a pronominal article without a separate name.

4:5.sourceText: Τότε παραλαμβάνει αὐτὸν ὁ διάβολος εἰς τὴν ἁγίαν πόλιν, καὶ ἔστησεν αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τὸ πτερύγιον τοῦ ἱεροῦ,
4:5.targetText: Then the devil took Him to the holy city and set Him on the pinnacle of the temple.

groups.note: Actual genitive article and temple noun together express the English genitive.

studyHeads.note: Actual genitive article supplies the local definite determiner.
Actual temple noun supplies the lexical head.

4:6.sourceText: καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ Εἰ Υἱὸς εἶ τοῦ Θεοῦ, βάλε σεαυτὸν κάτω· γέγραπται γὰρ ὅτι Τοῖς ἀγγέλοις αὐτοῦ ἐντελεῖται περὶ σοῦ καὶ ἐπὶ χειρῶν ἀροῦσίν σε, μή ποτε προσκόψῃς πρὸς λίθον τὸν πόδα σου.
4:6.targetText: “If You are the Son of God,” he said, “throw Yourself down. For it is written:  ‘He will command His angels concerning You, and they will lift You up in their hands, so that You will not strike Your foot against a stone.’”

groups.note: Actual third-plural raising supplies the English subject and phrasal action.
Exactly this actual object is lifted; the other written second-person occurrences carry their own separate roles.
Actual μή ποτε marks the negative-result clause. The English negative has a real written source.

studyHeads.note: Actual μή with adjacent ποτε introduces the negative circumstance.

groups.note: Actual second-singular striking supplies the grammatical subject and the recast finite form.

unmappedSource.reason: English leaves the introductory coordinator, dative speech recipient, and quotation introducer unexpressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the possessor of hands. The actual hands noun lacks an independently printed possessor.

4:7.sourceText: ἔφη αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Πάλιν γέγραπται Οὐκ ἐκπειράσεις Κύριον τὸν Θεόν σου.
4:7.targetText: Jesus replied, “It is also written: ‘Do not put the Lord your God to the test.’”

groups.note: Actual again here marks the additional quotation.
Actual perfect passive writing supplies the English passive expression.
Actual testing predicate supplies the English verbal construction, with the actual negator separately paired.

unmappedSource.reason: English does not separately express the actual dative speech addressee.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

4:8.sourceText: Πάλιν παραλαμβάνει αὐτὸν ὁ διάβολος εἰς ὄρος ὑψηλὸν λίαν, καὶ δείκνυσιν αὐτῷ πάσας τὰς βασιλείας τοῦ κόσμου καὶ τὴν δόξαν αὐτῶν,
4:8.targetText: Again, the devil took Him to a very high mountain and showed Him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory.

groups.note: Actual genitive article and world noun together express the English genitive.

studyHeads.note: Actual genitive article supplies this determiner.
Actual world noun supplies the head.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an indefinite article before the mountain.

4:9.sourceText: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ταῦτά σοι πάντα δώσω, ἐὰν πεσὼν προσκυνήσῃς μοι.
4:9.targetText: “All this I will give You,” he said, “if You will fall down and worship me.”

groups.note: Actual falling participle supplies the falling action in the shared conditional.
Actual second-singular worship subjunctive supplies the English subject and modal shared by the two actions.

unmappedSource.reason: English omits the actual narration connector and the dative speech recipient.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins falling and worship as verbal complements; the corresponding actual falling predicate is participial.

4:10.sourceText: τότε λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ὕπαγε, Σατανᾶ· γέγραπται γάρ Κύριον τὸν θεόν σου προσκυνήσεις καὶ αὐτῷ μόνῳ λατρεύσεις.
4:10.targetText: “Away from Me, Satan!” Jesus declared. “For it is written: ‘Worship the Lord your God and serve Him only.’”

groups.note: Actual present λέγει is recast as English past declared. The publisher row says told, while the installed edition writes declared.
Actual depart imperative supplies the elliptical English direction.

unmappedSource.reason: English leaves the actual then and the speech recipient without separate local wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English spells out the point of departure. There is no actual from-me phrase in this witness.

4:11.sourceText: Τότε ἀφίησιν αὐτὸν ὁ διάβολος, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄγγελοι προσῆλθον καὶ διηκόνουν αὐτῷ.
4:11.targetText: Then the devil left Him, and angels came and ministered to Him.

unmappedSource.reason: The written attention marker has no distinct expression in English.

4:12.sourceText: Ἀκούσας δὲ ὅτι Ἰωάνης παρεδόθη ἀνεχώρησεν εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν.
4:12.targetText: When Jesus heard that John had been imprisoned, He withdrew to Galilee.

groups.note: The actual hearing participle supplies the temporal English report.
The actual proper name is printed and denotes the person handed over. It is absent from the prior derived map despite the publisher’s source row.
Actual handed-over passive is rendered contextually as imprisonment in English; the actual παραδίδωμι remains the head.

unmappedSource.reason: The narrative connector is unexpressed. The English temporal When belongs to the hearing-participle frame.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the contextually identified hearer. No actual Jesus noun occurs in the verse.

4:13.sourceText: καὶ καταλιπὼν τὴν Ναζαρὰ ἐλθὼν κατῴκησεν εἰς Καφαρναοὺμ τὴν παραθαλασσίαν ἐν ὁρίοις Ζαβουλὼν καὶ Νεφθαλείμ·
4:13.targetText: Leaving Nazareth, He went and lived in Capernaum, which is by the sea in the region of Zebulun and Naphtali,

groups.note: Actual finite third-singular residence supplies the subject shared by went and lived in the English recasting.
The actual qualifying article makes the next adjective a modifier of Capernaum. English chooses a relative clause.
The actual place-name and publisher form preserve the same named territory despite spelling of the final syllable.

unmappedSource.reason: The initial narrative coordinator is unexpressed in English.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English coordinates participial arrival with the finite residence.
English supplies a copula when the actual qualifying article and adjective are expanded as a finite relative clause.

4:14.sourceText: ἵνα πληρωθῇ τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ Ἠσαΐου τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος
4:14.targetText: to fulfill what was spoken through the prophet Isaiah:

unmappedSource.reason: The actual saying participle following Isaiah is expressed by quotation punctuation rather than a word.

4:15.sourceText: Γῆ Ζαβουλὼν καὶ γῆ Νεφθαλείμ, ὁδὸν θαλάσσης, πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου, Γαλιλαία τῶν ἐθνῶν,
4:15.targetText: “Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, the Way of the Sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles—

groups.note: Actual proper name matches publisher Naphtali despite the spelling of the final Greek syllable.

4:16.sourceText: ὁ λαὸς ὁ καθήμενος ἐν σκοτίᾳ φῶς εἶδεν μέγα, καὶ τοῖς καθημένοις ἐν χώρᾳ καὶ σκιᾷ θανάτου φῶς ἀνέτειλεν αὐτοῖς.
4:16.targetText: the people living in darkness have seen a great light; on those living in the land of the shadow of death, a light has dawned.”

groups.note: The actual dative substantive article identifies the same group modified by the following participle.
Actual dative personal recipient is expressed by the fronted English dawn-on relation. The English noun phrase already expresses the same people.

unmappedSource.reason: English uses punctuation before the second clause and a nested shadow relation where Greek coordinates land and shadow.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

4:17.sourceText: Ἀπὸ τότε ἤρξατο ὁ Ἰησοῦς κηρύσσειν καὶ λέγειν Μετανοεῖτε, ἤγγικεν γὰρ ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν.
4:17.targetText: From that time on Jesus began to preach, “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is near.”

unmappedSource.reason: English quotation punctuation follows preach without an independent representation of the actual and-say expression.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

4:18.sourceText: Περιπατῶν δὲ παρὰ τὴν θάλασσαν τῆς Γαλιλαίας εἶδεν δύο ἀδελφούς, Σίμωνα τὸν λεγόμενον Πέτρον καὶ Ἀνδρέαν τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ, βάλλοντας ἀμφίβληστρον εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν· ἦσαν γὰρ ἁλεεῖς.
4:18.targetText: As Jesus was walking beside the Sea of Galilee, He saw two brothers, Simon called Peter and his brother Andrew. They were casting a net into the sea, for they were fishermen.

groups.note: The actual walking participle supplies the English temporal clause and its action.
Actual casting participle supplies the English finite spelling with the same people from the immediately preceding object.
Actual ἁλεεῖς and publisher ἁλιεῖς are the same fishermen noun, with the actual form and index retained.

unmappedSource.reason: English begins the temporal clause without the actual narrative connective.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: The actor is named explicitly in English; the actual participle is unnamed.
The English finite clause resumes the two brothers. The actual casting participle modifies them without a distinct pronoun.

4:19.sourceText: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Δεῦτε ὀπίσω μου, καὶ ποιήσω ὑμᾶς ἁλεεῖς ἀνθρώπων.
4:19.targetText: “Come, follow Me,” Jesus said, “and I will make you fishers of men.”

groups.note: Actual invitation comes with behind-me direction, rendered as follow in English. Actual behind adverb remains the source of the direction.

studyHeads.note: Actual behind supplies the following relation.

groups.note: Actual ἁλεεῖς and publisher ἁλιεῖς are the same fishing-person noun. Retain the actual written spelling.

unmappedSource.reason: English does not separately express the initial narrator connective and the actual speech recipients.

unmappedTarget.reason: English explicitly supplies the contextually identified speaker.

4:20.sourceText: οἱ δὲ εὐθέως ἀφέντες τὰ δίκτυα ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ.
4:20.targetText: And at once they left their nets and followed Him.

groups.note: The actual article functions pronominally as the subject in the contrastive construction.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English makes ownership of the nets explicit, with no actual possessive word.
English coordinates leaving and following. Actual leaving is dependent and no local coordinator introduces following.

4:21.sourceText: Καὶ προβὰς ἐκεῖθεν εἶδεν ἄλλους δύο ἀδελφούς, Ἰάκωβον τὸν τοῦ Ζεβεδαίου καὶ Ἰωάνην τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ, ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ μετὰ Ζεβεδαίου τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτῶν καταρτίζοντας τὰ δίκτυα αὐτῶν· καὶ ἐκάλεσεν αὐτούς.
4:21.targetText: Going on from there, He saw two other brothers, James son of Zebedee and his brother John. They were in a boat with their father Zebedee, mending their nets. Jesus called them,

groups.note: The actual John name and publisher row are explicit. The prior order-sensitive transfer skipped this name.

unmappedSource.reason: English omits the two independent narrative coordinators.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English expands the actual article with genitive Zebedee into a family noun. The actual Greek has no son noun.
English supplies the full location-clause subject and copula. The actual construction has a locative prepositional phrase.
English supplies the named contextually identified actor of the actual call.

4:22.sourceText: οἱ δὲ εὐθέως ἀφέντες τὸ πλοῖον καὶ τὸν πατέρα αὐτῶν ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ.
4:22.targetText: and immediately they left the boat and their father and followed Him.

groups.note: The actual article functions pronominally as the subject of the response.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English coordinates leaving and following in its finite recasting, with no separate actual coordinator before following.

4:23.sourceText: Καὶ περιῆγεν ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ Γαλιλαίᾳ, διδάσκων ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς αὐτῶν καὶ κηρύσσων τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τῆς βασιλείας καὶ θεραπεύων πᾶσαν νόσον καὶ πᾶσαν μαλακίαν ἐν τῷ λαῷ.
4:23.targetText: Jesus went throughout Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing every disease and sickness among the people.

groups.note: The actual in-all expression is rendered by the English extent preposition.

studyHeads.note: Actual whole supplies the extent of the relation.

groups.note: The two actual every qualifiers apply to disease and sickness separately. English expresses the same shared scope once.

studyHeads.note: The first actual qualifier begins the scope of this English shared quantifier.

unmappedSource.reason: English omits the opening connective and uses a comma where the written conjunction precedes preaching.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the name of the contextual subject of went.

4:24.sourceText: καὶ ἀπῆλθεν ἡ ἀκοὴ αὐτοῦ εἰς ὅλην τὴν Συρίαν· καὶ προσήνεγκαν αὐτῷ πάντας τοὺς κακῶς ἔχοντας ποικίλαις νόσοις καὶ βασάνοις συνεχομένους, δαιμονιζομένους καὶ σεληνιαζομένους καὶ παραλυτικούς, καὶ ἐθεράπευσεν αὐτούς.
4:24.targetText: News about Him spread all over Syria, and people brought to Him all who were ill with various diseases, those suffering acute pain, the demon-possessed, those having seizures, and the paralyzed—and He healed them.

groups.note: Actual badly-having expresses illness. English gives a finite predicate and an added preposition for the disease relation.

studyHeads.note: The actual having participle supplies the predication in the idiom.
Actual badly contributes the illness sense in the idiom.
English expresses the illness relationship around actual having.

unmappedSource.reason: English omits the opening narrative coordinator and two list coordinators, giving the affected groups with punctuation.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

4:25.sourceText: καὶ ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ ὄχλοι πολλοὶ ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας καὶ Δεκαπόλεως καὶ Ἱεροσολύμων καὶ Ἰουδαίας καὶ πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου.
4:25.targetText: The large crowds that followed Him came from Galilee, the Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judea, and beyond the Jordan.

groups.note: Actual ἀπό introduces the places of origin. English supplies came from rather than the Greek crowds from those places.

unmappedSource.reason: English omits the introductory connective and expresses the first three listed transitions with punctuation.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds a definite determiner to the crowds noun.
English recasts the actual finite following predicate as a relative description.
English supplies an explicit movement predicate with the origin locations. The actual movement verb is following, already linked to followed.
